newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes higher against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes higher against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed higher at 8.2940 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday from Monday's 8.2947 with strong support seen above the 8.2950 level, dealers said.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2947.
Dealers said active buying emerged which strengthened pro-yuan sentiment considerably.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2945 and consolidated around that level, hitting an intraday low of 8.2947 early in trading.
It then rose slightly, hitting a high of 8.2895 late in trading.
Trading was sluggish with some of the major banks showing little interest in entering the market, dealers said.
"The yuan will maintain its upward trend in the next few days since there is no major negative news is in sight to change it," said one dealer. "But a technical correction may emerge at some point."
"Active buying was seen at the key support level of 8.2950, indicating strong pro-yuan sentiment," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to fall slightly on Tuesday after the successive gains of recent sessions.
The yuan closed down at an intraday low of 6.6000 from 6.5431 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly up at 1.0698 from 1.0700 against the Hong Kong dollar.
